entries.originalText: Lord, be thou my help in trouble, for vain is the help of man.(1) How often have I failed to find faithfulness, where I thought I possessed it.
entries.modernizedText: Lord, be my help in trouble, for vain is the help of man.(1) How often I have failed to find faithfulness where I thought I had it.

entries.originalText: How many times I have found it where I least expected.
entries.modernizedText: How many times I have found it where I least expected it.

entries.originalText: Vain therefore is hope in men, but the salvation of the just, O God, is in Thee.
entries.modernizedText: Hope in people is vain, therefore, but the salvation of the just, O God, is in You.

entries.originalText: Blessed be thou, O Lord my God, in all things which happen unto us.
entries.modernizedText: Blessed be You, O Lord my God, in all that happens to us.

entries.originalText: We are weak and unstable, we are quickly deceived and quite changed.
entries.modernizedText: We are weak and unstable; we are quickly deceived and completely changed.

entries.originalText: Who is the man who is able to keep himself so warily and circumspectly as not sometimes to come into some snare of perplexity?
entries.modernizedText: Who can guard himself so carefully and cautiously that he never falls into some snare of confusion?

entries.originalText: But he who trusteth in Thee, O Lord, and seeketh Thee with an unfeigned heart, doth not so easily slip.
entries.modernizedText: But whoever trusts in You, O Lord, and seeks You with a sincere heart does not slip so easily.

entries.originalText: And if he fall into any tribulation, howsoever he may be entangled, yet very quickly he shall be delivered through Thee, or by Thee shall be comforted, because Thou wilt not forsake him that trusteth in Thee unto the end.
entries.modernizedText: And if he falls into any trouble, however entangled he may be, he will very quickly be delivered through You or comforted by You, because You will not forsake the one who trusts in You to the end.

entries.originalText: A friend who continueth faithful in all the distresses of his friend is rare to be found.
entries.modernizedText: A friend who remains faithful through all the troubles of his friend is rare.

entries.originalText: Thou, O Lord, Thou alone art most faithful in all things, and there is none other like unto Thee.
entries.modernizedText: You, O Lord, You alone are most faithful in all things, and there is no one like You.

entries.originalText: Oh, how truly wise was that holy soul which said, “My mind is steadfastly fixed, and it is grounded in Christ.”(2) If thus it were with me, the fear of man should not so easily tempt me, nor the arrows of words move me.
entries.modernizedText: Oh, how truly wise was that holy soul who said, “My mind is steadfastly fixed, and it is grounded in Christ.”(2) If it were so with me, fear of others would not tempt me so easily, nor would the arrows of words move me.

entries.originalText: Who is sufficient to foresee all things, who to guard beforehand against future ills?
entries.modernizedText: Who is able to foresee all things, or to guard beforehand against future evils?

entries.originalText: If even things which are foreseen sometimes hurt us, what can things which are not foreseen do, but grievously injure?
entries.modernizedText: If even things we foresee sometimes hurt us, what can things we do not foresee do but grievously injure us?

entries.originalText: But wherefore have I not better provided for myself, miserable that I am?
entries.modernizedText: But why have I not made better provision for myself, miserable as I am?

entries.originalText: Why, too, have I given such heed to others?
entries.modernizedText: Why, too, have I paid such attention to others?

entries.originalText: But we are men, nor are we other than frail men, even though by many we are reckoned and called angels.
entries.modernizedText: But we are human, nothing more than frail human beings, even though many regard and call us angels.

entries.originalText: Whom shall I trust, O Lord, whom shall I trust but Thee?
entries.modernizedText: Whom shall I trust, O Lord, whom shall I trust but You?

entries.originalText: Thou art the Truth, and deceivest not, nor canst be deceived.
entries.modernizedText: You are the Truth and do not deceive, nor can You be deceived.

entries.originalText: And on the other hand, Every man is a liar,(3) weak, unstable and frail, especially in his words, so that one ought scarcely ever to believe what seemeth to sound right on the face of it.
entries.modernizedText: And on the other hand, Every man is a liar,(3) weak, unstable, and frail, especially in his words, so that one should scarcely ever believe what seems right on its face.

entries.originalText: With what wisdom hast thou warned us beforehand to beware of men, and that a man’s foes are they of his own household,(4) and that we must not believe if one say unto us Lo here, or Lo there.(5) I have been taught by my loss, and O that I may prove more careful and not foolish hereby.
entries.modernizedText: How wisely You have warned us beforehand to beware of people, and that a person’s enemies are those of his own household,(4) and that we must not believe if someone says to us, Look here, or Look there.(5) I have been taught by my loss, and may I become more careful and not foolish through it.

entries.originalText: “Be cautious,” saith some one: “be cautious, keep unto thyself what I tell thee.”
entries.modernizedText: “Be cautious,” someone says; “be cautious, keep to yourself what I tell you.”

entries.originalText: And whilst I am silent and believe that it is hid with me, he himself cannot keep silence concerning it, but straightway betrayeth me and himself, and goeth his way.
entries.modernizedText: And while I am silent and believe that the matter is hidden with me, he himself cannot keep silent about it, but immediately betrays me and himself and goes on his way.

entries.originalText: Protect me, O Lord, from such mischief-making and reckless men; let me not fall into their hands, nor ever do such things myself.
entries.modernizedText: Protect me, O Lord, from such troublemaking and reckless people; do not let me fall into their hands or ever do such things myself.

entries.originalText: Put a true and steadfast word into my mouth, and remove a deceitful tongue far from me.
entries.modernizedText: Put a true and steadfast word into my mouth, and remove a deceitful tongue far from me.

entries.originalText: What I would not suffer, I ought by all means to beware of doing.
entries.modernizedText: What I would not endure, I ought by all means to beware of doing.

entries.originalText: Oh, how good and peacemaking a thing it is to be silent concerning others, and not carelessly to believe all reports, nor to hand them on further; how good also to lay one’s self open to few, to seek ever to have Thee as the beholder of the heart; not to be carried about with every wind of words, but to desire that all things inward and outward be done according to the good pleasure of Thy will!
entries.modernizedText: Oh, how good and peaceable it is to be silent about others, not carelessly to believe every report or pass it on; how good also to confide in few, always to seek You as the witness of the heart, not to be carried about by every wind of words, but to desire that all things inward and outward be done according to the good pleasure of Your will!

entries.originalText: How safe for the preserving of heavenly grace to fly from human approval, and not to long after the things which seem to win admiration abroad, but to follow with all earnestness those things which bring amendment of life and heavenly fervour!
entries.modernizedText: How safe it is for preserving heavenly grace to flee human approval and not long for things that seem to win admiration abroad, but to pursue with all earnestness those things that bring amendment of life and heavenly fervor!

entries.originalText: How many have been injured by their virtue being made known and too hastily praised.
entries.modernizedText: How many have been harmed by having their virtue made known and too quickly praised.

entries.originalText: How truly profitable hath been grace preserved in silence in this frail life, which, as we are told, is all temptation and warfare.
entries.modernizedText: How truly profitable grace has been when preserved in silence in this frail life, which, as we are told, is all temptation and warfare.
